sanskrit_verse:
कृषिः शिल्पं भृतिर्विद्या कुसीदं शकटं गिरिः ।
सेवानूपं नृपो भैक्षम् आपत्तौ जीवनानि तु ॥
transliteration:
kṛṣiḥ śilpaṃ bhṛtir vidyā kusīdaṃ śakaṭaṃ giriḥ /
sevānūpaṃ nṛpo bhaikṣam āpattau jīvanāni tu //
sph_interpretive_translation: In times of crisis, all livelihoods—farming, craftsmanship, service, learning, trade, transport, mountainry, pastoral care, governance, and begging—are valid means of sustenance.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from adaptability in dharma during crisis
Causation aligns with survival-consciousness, not structural norms
Capacity-based responsibility expands to include all viable roles
Restoration logic activates when existential threat arises
Consciousness alignment occurs through necessity-driven action
executable_legal_axioms: IF societal collapse OR individual survival risk detected THEN ALL lawful livelihoods VALIDATED
IF crisis declared BY competent authority THEN occupational hierarchy SUSPENDED
IF person engages in ANY dharmic labor FOR sustenance THEN no liability INCURRED
IF governance fails THEN decentralized subsistence modes ENABLED automatically
supreme_court_application: Supreme judicial authority recognizes that in systemic breakdown, all prior economic hierarchies dissolve. The court must affirm survival-based activity as constitutionally protected, overriding peacetime regulatory frameworks.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa confirms that necessity dissolves artificial boundaries; anupūrvaśaḥ shows how survival precedes social order; proportional responsibility lies in acting according to capacity; non-punitive reality upholds life above convention.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Realign community resource access based on immediate need
Restore local production capacity without bureaucratic interference
Establish peer-based integrity verification for crisis-based roles
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam: In crisis, all dharmic work becomes sacred duty. There is no sin in survival. Dharma is restored through recognition of necessity's sovereignty. Consciousness alone adjudicates rightly.
